thesis.PETR4: The federal government controls the vote. Fuel prices, investment pace, and dividend policy shift with whoever is in power — and that shows up in the multiple before it shows up in earnings.
thesis.BBAS3: Trades at a structural discount to private banks on political-balance-sheet risk (directed credit, farm subsidies). A government seen as capital-discipline friendly compresses that discount.
thesis.CMIG4: Controlled by Minas Gerais state. Every election cycle reopens privatization, dividends, and using the company as a fiscal tool for the state.
thesis.AXIA3: The former Eletrobras, renamed. Privatized, but with an open fight over the federal government’s voting power. The electric name where the election thesis is still more legal than operational.
thesis.CPLE3: Privatized Paraná utility. Generation, transmission, and distribution in one group: the multiple reacts to tariffs, hydrology, and the discount the market still charges for its state origins.
thesis.EQTL3: Distributor that grows by buying hard concessions and cutting losses and delinquency. An execution thesis, not a Brasília thesis.
thesis.ENGI11: Same model as Equatorial: distribution in high-loss regions, leveraged to operating improvement and the rate cycle.
thesis.CPFE3: Controlled by State Grid. Distribution and generation with more predictable cash flow than state-owned peers — the price follows rates and tariffs, not election polls.
thesis.EGIE3: Contracted generation controlled by France’s Engie. An income profile: what moves it is the real rate, because the dividend competes with Tesouro IPCA+.
thesis.ENEV3: Gas-fired thermal generation. Not Copel’s power bill: results depend on dispatch, gas, and contracts — more commodity than tariff.
thesis.ALUP11: Transmission in Brazil and Peru. Contracted revenue, inflation in the contract: the direct competitor is Tesouro IPCA+, not the Ibovespa.
thesis.ISAE4: Transmission (ex-Transmissão Paulista). Same logic as Taesa: high rates compress the multiple even with a stable contract.
thesis.AURE3: Renewable generation spun out of Votorantim. Still trades like a company being built: a low price can be an execution discount, not a margin of safety.
thesis.SBSP3: Privatized under a state government. Tariffs and the sanitation framework depend on regulation, so political risk is real — but state and regulatory, not federal.
thesis.B3SA3: Earns on traded volume. The purest way to bet on falling rates: a lower Selic pushes investors from fixed income into equities, and B3 takes a toll on every trade.
thesis.ITUB4: Exposed to the credit cycle and Selic, without the state bank’s political discount. Reacts to elections through macro (rates, defaults), not through ownership control.
thesis.BBDC4: Same logic as Itaú, with a book historically more sensitive to defaults — which amplifies a rate-cycle move.
thesis.SANB11: Controlled by Spain’s Santander. The discount vs Itaú usually comes from profitability, not political risk — so cheap here is an execution thesis, not an election one.
thesis.BRSR6: Rio Grande do Sul state bank. Thinner liquidity, a state-control discount, and a regionally concentrated book — the low multiple is often structural, not an obvious opportunity.
thesis.ABCB4: Mid-size wholesale bank. Neither a private giant’s umbrella nor a state bank’s political discount: the price follows the credit cycle and funding.
thesis.BMGB4: Focused on payroll loans and low-income retail. A low P/B usually tracks a high cost of capital and credit risk — looks like a banana, expensive if defaults widen.
thesis.BPAC11: Investment bank: revenue depends on issuance, M&A, and asset management. All of that reopens when the cost of capital falls.
thesis.VALE3: Dollar revenue from iron ore. China and FX explain far more of the stock price than any election poll.
thesis.GGBR4: Steel has a domestic leg (construction) and a U.S. leg. High rates here hurt, but U.S. results cushion local political risk.
thesis.WEGE3: Brazilian multinational selling motors and electrical equipment worldwide. The thesis is execution and the dollar, not Brasília.
thesis.EMBJ3: Dollar order book and defense exposure. Government matters as a customer and trade diplomacy, not as a controlling shareholder.
thesis.SUZB3: Pulp is a global dollar commodity. Historically a hedge: when political risk weakens the real, revenue rises in reais.
thesis.PRIO3: Oil without the state on the board. Useful to separate what in PETR4 is Brent from what is political risk.
thesis.TAEE11: Transmission with contracted, inflation-linked revenue. Competes directly with CDI: when Selic rises, the dividend looks less attractive and the stock falls.
thesis.VIVT3: Predictable, defensive cash flow. Political risk is regulatory (auctions, tariffs), not ownership control.
thesis.ABEV3: Staple consumption with low leverage. What moves it is household income and tax reform on beverages.
thesis.RADL3: Defensive retail: medicine gets bought in any scenario. Still hurt by high rates, because growth is worth less when discounted at 14%.
thesis.LREN3: Discretionary retail is the most sensitive gauge of rates and income. Often among the first to react when the yield curve opens or closes.
thesis.RENT3: Capital-intensive model funded by debt. Effectively a leveraged bet on the path of Selic.
